## PDF page 25

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=25)

```text
                               R A N G E B UI L DI N G


players call 2bets with, and then there are 8 re-raising ranges. This is not
to say that these ranges are perfect, or even ranges that you should use.
The goal is to get acclimated with pairing actual ranges of hands with their
respective %-form.

TOOLS TO USE: Flopzilla, Equilab, and PokerCruncher will work well.

PROCESS: Plug the range into your software of choice (again, you can copy/
paste the range strand to save yourself some time) and jot down the %-form
for each one. Keep in mind that the location of the %-form may vary slightly
in your software of choice, but normally it is near the range slider.




TAKEAWAYS: The value of this exercise, beyond expanding your technical
knowledge, is to uncover some patterns when it comes to how wide a range
is (larger %-forms are looser and smaller %-forms are tighter). This ties beau-
tifully together with frequencies as well. If a player open-raises 15% of hands,
and you have a solid idea of what a range that includes the top 15% of hands
looks like, you have essentially done the heavy lifting of preflop hand reading.

GLGL.




                                     PA G E 2 5
```
